ff_news.extrait: Before beginning my speech, I would like to offer my heartfelt sympathies to those who are suffering from the recent heavy rain. A little over a year has passed since I was appointed as a member of the Policy Board. During this time, the whole world has wrestled with two major issues related to the United States: one concerning tariffs and the other concerning the Iran situation. The tariff issue, unexpectedly, did not cause any economic disruption in Japan, although it did impact primarily sectors that have high export volumes to the United States, such as automobiles. In contrast, the Iran situation has had far broader repercussions. The supply of crude oil and other materials has tightened due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. This could induce both a rise in inflation and a deceleration in economic activity, placing central banks worldwide in a difficult decision-making environment. In terms of the impact on Japan, crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) have shown different price dynamics. Crude oil prices have risen due to a shortage of supply, whereas LNG prices have increased even without such a shortage. ff_news.extrait_fr: Avant de commencer mon discours, je voudrais offrir mes plus sincères condoléances à ceux qui souffrent des fortes pluies récentes. Un peu plus d’un an s’est écoulé depuis que j’ai été nommé membre du Conseil d’orientation. Pendant ce temps, le monde entier a été aux prises avec deux problèmes majeurs liés aux États-Unis : l’un concernant les droits de douane et l’autre concernant la situation en Iran. Contre toute attente, la question des droits de douane n'a provoqué aucune perturbation économique au Japon, même si elle a principalement touché les secteurs qui exportent de gros volumes vers les États-Unis, comme l'automobile. En revanche, la situation iranienne a eu des répercussions bien plus vastes. L'approvisionnement en pétrole brut et autres matières premières s'est resserré en raison de la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz. Cela pourrait entraîner à la fois une hausse de l’inflation et un ralentissement de l’activité économique, plaçant les banques centrales du monde entier dans un environnement décisionnel difficile. En termes d’impact sur le Japon, le pétrole brut et le gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL) ont affiché des dynamiques de prix différentes. Les prix du pétrole brut ont augmenté en raison d’une pénurie d’approvisionnement, tandis que les prix du GNL ont augmenté même sans une telle pénurie. Masu, membre du conseil d'administration de la CBoJ : la BoJ continuera probablement à augmenter les taux d'intérêt dans le contexte de conditions financières souples actuelles, Masu, membre du conseil d'administration de la Banque du Japon : l'inflation sous-jacente reste inférieure à 2 % mais proche de ce niveau. Masu : le rythme et le calendrier des hausses de taux de la BOJ dépendront de la probabilité de respecter les projections et les risques de référence, en tenant compte de l'évolution des prix du pétrole, de la demande mondiale et des fluctuations monétaires.

cb_articles.contenu_fr:
Les commentaires de Masu s'ajoutent à une tendance belliciste déjà en train de se développer parmi les membres du conseil d'administration de la BoJ avant la réunion de septembre, renforçant les attentes du marché selon lesquelles une hausse est probable, en fait fondamentalement gravée dans le marbre. Son accent particulier sur l'impact plus important de la faiblesse du yen sur l'inflation que par le passé, ainsi que les inquiétudes concernant les prix à la production qui se répercutent sur l'inflation à la consommation plus que par le passé, donnent au yen un certain soutien à la marge, car cela indique que le conseil d'administration ne se contente pas de réagir aux coûts énergétiques globaux, mais de construire un argumentaire plus large en faveur d'une normalisation politique.

Le taux directeur étant déjà décrit comme se rapprochant de la fourchette neutre estimée, le signal le plus sensible au marché pourrait être le commentaire de Masu selon lequel la BOJ pourrait être contrainte de relever rapidement les taux si l'inflation s'accélère, ce qui accroît les enjeux autour de la publication des données à venir d'ici la réunion, et au-delà.

---

Plus tôt :

---

Un membre du conseil d'administration de la BoJ, qui a déjà appelé à des hausses anticipées, affirme que les arguments en faveur de la poursuite de la hausse des taux ne cessent de se renforcer, et non de s'affaiblir.

Résumé :

Kazuyuki Masu, membre du conseil d'administration de la Banque du Japon, a déclaré que l'inflation sous-jacente restait inférieure à l'objectif de 2% de la banque centrale, mais qu'elle en était désormais assez proche, ajoutant que la BoJ devrait continuer à relever ses taux d'intérêt compte tenu des conditions financières toujours accommodantes. Ses commentaires interviennent avant la prochaine réunion politique de la BoJ les 17 et 18 septembre, au cours de laquelle les marchés s'attendent généralement à une nouvelle hausse des taux.

Masu, ancien directeur financier de la maison de négoce Mitsubishi Corp, a rejoint le conseil d'administration de la BOJ en juillet 2025, occupant un siège traditionnellement réservé aux dirigeants d'entreprise. Il est généralement considéré comme l’un des membres les plus bellicistes du conseil d’administration actuel. Il a voté en faveur du maintien des taux inchangés lors de la réunion d'avril de la BoJ, mais a déclaré le mois suivant qu'il pensait que les taux devraient augmenter dès que possible à condition qu'il n'y ait pas de signes clairs de ralentissement économique. Ses commentaires sont donc cohérents avec cette position plutôt qu'un changement de position.

Sur le fond, Masu a déclaré que le rythme et le calendrier de nouvelles hausses de taux dépendraient de la probabilité de réalisation des projections d'inflation de base de la BoJ, ainsi que des risques liés aux prix du pétrole, à la demande liée à l'IA et aux fluctuations monétaires. Il a déclaré que la considération la plus importante était d’éviter un dépassement brutal de l’inflation sous-jacente au-dessus de l’objectif de 2 %. Il a également abordé directement la hausse actuelle des coûts de l'énergie, affirmant que même si une hausse des prix des carburants et des produits chimiques pourrait s'avérer être un choc ponctuel, elle pourrait néanmoins avoir un impact plus large sur les prix à travers les coûts de distribution, et a souligné séparément l'inquiétude selon laquelle la hausse des coûts résultant du conflit au Moyen-Orient pourrait faire augmenter les prix globaux comme une tendance durable plutôt que temporaire.

Masu a souligné plusieurs pressions supplémentaires qui méritent d'être surveillées, notamment une récente hausse de 7 % des prix à la production, qui, selon lui, pourrait se répercuter sur l'inflation à la consommation plus que par le passé, ainsi qu'une réaccélération attendue des prix alimentaires qu'il a décrite comme potentiellement essentielle aux perspectives d'inflation à long terme. Il a également déclaré que la faiblesse du yen avait un impact plus important sur l'inflation que par le passé et méritait donc une attention particulière, et a séparément noté aucun signe pour l'instant que les récentes hausses de taux freinent l'appétit des entreprises pour les fonds, ajoutant qu'il surveillait les signes d'une possible surchauffe des investissements des entreprises.

Concernant le cadre politique lui-même, Masu a déclaré que le Japon n'était plus en déflation et que la BoJ devait faire sortir son taux d'intérêt réel du territoire négatif dès que possible. Alors que le taux directeur se rapproche désormais de la fourchette neutre estimée par la BoJ, il a déclaré que la banque centrale devait surveiller attentivement les prix, l'emploi et les conditions financières, et a averti que si l'inflation s'accélérait, la BoJ pourrait être contrainte de relever ses taux plus rapidement que prévu actuellement. Il a également signalé une question distincte, à plus long terme, à laquelle se trouve confrontée la BoJ, à savoir quelle fourchette d'échéances des obligations d'État japonaises elle devrait continuer à détenir, compte tenu de la taille souhaitable de son bilan.
cb_articles.contenu:
Masu's comments add to a hawkish tilt already building among BOJ board members ahead of the September meeting, reinforcing market expectations that a hike is likely, indeed abasically set in stone. His specific focus on the weak yen having a bigger inflation impact than in the past, alongside concern about producer prices feeding through to consumer inflation more than historically,gives the yen some supporton the margin, since it signals the board is not just reacting to headline energy costs but building a broader case for policy normalisation.

With the policy rate already described as approaching the estimated neutral range, the more market sensitive signal here may be Masu's comment that the BOJ could be forced to raise rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, which raises the stakes around upcoming data releases between now and the meeting, and beyond.

---

Earlier:

---

A BOJ board member who has already called for early hikes says the case for continuing to raise rates keeps getting stronger, not weaker.

Summary:

Bank of Japan board member Kazuyuki Masu said underlying inflation remains below the central bank's 2% target but is now quite close to it, adding that the BOJ is expected to continue raising interest rates given how accommodative financial conditions remain. His comments come ahead of the BOJ's next policy meeting on September 17 and 18, which markets widely expect to produce a further rate hike.

Masu, a former chief financial officer at trading house Mitsubishi Corp, joined the BOJ board in July 2025, filling a seat traditionally reserved for a business executive. He is generally regarded as one of the more hawkish members of the current board. He voted to keep rates unchanged at the BOJ's April meeting, but said the following month that he believed rates should rise as soon as possible provided there were no clear signs of an economic slowdown, so his comments are consistent with that stance rather than a shift in it.

On the substance, Masu said the pace and timing of further rate increases would depend on the likelihood of achieving the BOJ's baseline inflation projections, alongside risks tied to oil prices, AI related demand and currency fluctuations. He said the most important consideration is avoiding a sharp overshoot of underlying inflation above the 2% target. He also addressed the current run up in energy costs directly, saying that while a rise in fuel and chemical goods prices could prove to be a one off shock, it may still have a broader impact on prices through distribution costs, and separately flagged concern that rising costs stemming from the Middle East conflict could push up overall prices as a lasting trend rather than a temporary one.

Masu pointed to several additional pressures worth watching, including a recent 7% spike in producer prices, which he said could feed through to consumer inflation more than it has historically, alongside an expected reacceleration in food prices that he described as potentially key to the long term inflation outlook. He also said the weak yen is having a larger impact on inflation than in the past and therefore warrants close attention, and separately noted no sign yet that recent rate hikes are denting corporate appetite for funds, adding he was watching for signs that corporate investment could be overheating.

On the policy framework itself, Masu said Japan is no longer in deflation and that the BOJ must move its real interest rate out of negative territory as soon as possible. With the policy rate now approaching the BOJ's estimated neutral range, he said the central bank needs to watch price, job and financial conditions carefully, and warned that if inflation accelerates, the BOJ could be forced to raise rates more rapidly than currently anticipated. He also flagged a separate, longer term question facing the BOJ over which maturity range of Japanese government bonds it should continue holding as it considers the desirable size of its balance sheet.
cb_articles.titre: Weak yen, oil costs and food prices in focus as BOJ's Masu talks hikes

cb_articles.titre: PBOC sets USD/ CNY reference rate for today at 6.7766 (vs. estimate at 6.7074)

cb_articles.contenu:
The fixing mechanism matters most right now because of what it has been signalling over recent weeks. The PBOC set its reference rate at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months in late August, after the yuan touched a three and a half year high, a clear sign of discomfort with the pace of gains rather than the level itself. Traders should read this as the central bank applying the brakes rather than attempting to reverse the broader trend, since the yuan has still risen a meaningful amount against the dollar this year. The balancing act Beijing faces is straightforward: a stronger currency helps with capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness at a time when the domestic economy is showing renewed signs of softness. Watching the gap between the daily fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the more reliable ways to gauge PBOC intent in the days ahead.

---

Earlier:

---The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and lately the message has been to slow down.

Summary:

The People's Bank of China sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT, a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets, and one that has taken on added significance in recent weeks as policymakers work to manage the pace of the yuan's rise.

China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the yuan is allowed to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the central midpoint set each trading day. That midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies such as the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic considerations like capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The calculation is not purely mechanical, giving policymakers room to use the fixing to guide market expectations.

Once the midpoint is set, onshore USD/CNY trades freely within the allowable range. Should market pressure push the currency toward either edge of that band, the central bank can step in to smooth volatility, whether through direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance channelled through state owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often read as a policy signal rather than a purely technical reference point. A stronger than expected midpoint typically suggests the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can signal tolerance for a softer currency, often in response to dollar strength or domestic headwinds.

This dynamic has played out clearly over the past couple of weeks. In late August, the PBOC set its fixing at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months, coming shortly after the yuan touched a three and a half year high against the dollar. The move was widely read as a sign of unease with the speed of the currency's advance rather than its overall direction, with analysts describing the central bank as applying the brakes rather than reversing the trend. The yuan had still gained a meaningful amount against the dollar this year at that point, underscoring that Beijing's concern was pace rather than level.

The underlying tension is a familiar one. A firmer yuan supports capital stability and eases import costs, but a rapid rise risks undermining export competitiveness at a moment when China's broader economy continues to show signs of softness. For traders and investors, the gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest windows into how Beijing is currently weighing that trade off.
cb_articles.titre: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7074 – Reuters estimate

cb_articles.contenu:
With ING pencilling in a 25 basis point hike across every scenario it considers, today's meeting is likely to be less about the rate decision itself and more about the accompanying language and projections. The spread ING lays out between its most dovish and most hawkish outcomes, EUR/USD ranging from 1.150 to 1.168 and the 10 year Bund yield from 3.30% to 3.45%, points to meaningful two way risk around the press conference rather than the decision itself. Given the euro and Bund currently sit close to the middle of that range, at 1.161 and 3.40% respectively, positioning into the announcement looks reasonably balanced, leaving room for a sharp move once the tone of the guidance becomes clear.

---

Earlier:

---

ING thinks the ECB's rate move today is close to a formality, it is the tone of the guidance that will actually move markets.

Summary:

ING expects the European Central Bank to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points at today's meeting regardless of which way the tone of the accompanying guidance breaks, according to a scenario framework the bank published ahead of the decision. The current depo rate stands at 2.25%, with the ECB maintaining a data dependent, meeting by meeting approach heading into the announcement.

The bank's note, illustrated in an accompanying graphic, sets out four possible outcomes built around inflation, growth and the tone of interest rate guidance. In the current stance, ING sees upside risks to inflation from higher energy prices and the possibility of second round effects, while growth risks remain tilted to the downside in the near term because of the war in the Middle East.

At the dovish end of the spectrum, ING's very dovish scenario has the ECB delivering the expected hike while signalling a prolonged pause and voicing concern about bond market conditions, a combination the bank associates with a weaker euro near 1.150 and a 10 year Bund yield around 3.30%. ING's own base case sits just above that in a dovish hike scenario, where inflation projections are revised slightly higher without shifting the broader balance of risk, growth forecasts improve while downside risks linger, and policymakers offer only a slight pushback against market pricing while keeping their options open. That scenario is associated with EUR/USD near 1.157 and a Bund yield around 3.35%.

Moving toward the hawkish end, a neutral scenario would see the ECB acknowledge that the latest escalation in the region is adding fresh upside inflation risk, while treating growth risks as more balanced following improved projections, and signalling that another hike in the coming months remains possible. ING pairs that outcome with EUR/USD around 1.163 and a Bund yield near 3.40%, close to where both currently trade. In its most hawkish scenario, ING sees the ECB acknowledging that the inflation impact may be larger than initially thought, requiring continued policy action, alongside a bigger than expected upward revision to growth projections, with clear hints of a further hike in October and potentially beyond. That outcome carries the highest levels in ING's framework, with EUR/USD near 1.168 and the Bund yield around 3.45%.

With the euro and Bund currently trading closest to ING's neutral case, the bank's framework suggests markets are already leaning toward the view that today's hike will come with a firmer tone rather than a dovish one, leaving scope for a larger reaction if the ECB's guidance ultimately lands closer to either extreme of ING's range.

il_articles.contenu:
investingLive.com has prepared for you stock investors aU.S. earnings sentimentthrough September 9, 2026

Recent U.S. earnings reactions suggest investors are becoming less forgiving. Nearly half the stocks in the latest completed group rose, yet several influential disappointments pulled the overall picture lower. Technology and consumer shares showed particular weakness, while meaningful winners remained. The evidence points to a selective, increasingly defensive market.

The distinction is betweenhow many stocks fallandhow much damage those declines cause.

The September 9 earnings-reaction picture showed:

The equal-weight average treats every stock equally. The market-cap-weighted figure gives larger companies more influence. The median describes the stock in the middle of the group.

What stands out to me is the gap between the nearly flat equal-weight result and the much weaker result when company size matters. That suggests a few influential disappointments are weighing heavily on sentiment.

These are figures for the reviewed earnings group, not returns for the entire U.S. stock market.

Timing also matters. Companies reporting on September 9 before the opening bell produced healthier reactions on their own. Weakness among companies that reported after the previous close pulled down the combined picture.

Several declines were substantial. Casey’s General Stores (CASY) fell about14%, ServiceTitan (TTAN) approximately30%, and Chewy (CHWY) nearly11%on September 9.

Yet buyers were still willing to reward other companies. Signet Jewelers and Academy Sports posted strong advances, while Sunbelt Rentals also gained, illustrating the range of outcomes within the same reporting group.

A major negative contributor such as Casey’s had an outsized influence on the overall result. That reinforces the concentration of the weakness. It does not make the losses unimportant, but it limits how broadly we should interpret them.

There was another warning: more stocks made large downside moves beyond the options market’s expected range than made comparable upside moves. In plain language, negative surprises were more likely to exceed the size of move traders had priced in.

A falling stock price does not automatically mean a company’s earnings or revenue declined.

ServiceTitan, for example, reported21% year-over-year revenue growthin its latest quarter, even as its shares suffered a severe selloff. That growth is documented in the company’sfiscal second-quarter results.

Investors assess results against what they expected and what the share price already assumed. They also consider management’s outlook for future business.

A company can therefore report growth and still disappoint the market. Equally, a business facing difficulties can rally if its results or outlook prove better than feared.

My reading of the latest reactions is that investors’ tolerance for disappointment is narrowing. That is a warning about expectations and positioning; these price moves alone do not establish a broad deterioration in corporate profits.

The latest earnings group showed a clear sector divide:

These observations describe recent reporters, rather than every company in each sector.

Signet and Academy Sports are particularly useful reminders that even a weaker consumer group can contain strong winners. Sector direction helps frame a watchlist, but individual company reactions still matter.

This connects with investingLive’s discussion ofcrowded technology leadership and improving Materials: investors benefit from looking beyond the most visible market theme when assessing where strength is developing.

The recent technology picture shows considerable dispersion.

As of September 9, approximaterolling five-trading-day returnsamong recent reporters included:

These are rolling returns, not returns measured from each company’s earnings release.They show how these stocks performed over a common recent window, which may include trading before and after their reports.

The contrast suggests investors are making sharper distinctions among technology and AI-related businesses. Dell and HPE provide meaningful counterexamples to the weakness elsewhere.

For traders, the useful question is whether a particular company can meet demanding expectations and sustain buying interest after the initial reaction.

The initial September 9 after-hours earnings group added another cautionary signal. Only aboutone quarterof the group traded higher, while larger-company reactions leaned heavily negative.

However, that group was not dominated by the largest U.S. mega-cap companies. Its broader market significance was therefore limited.

These were also preliminary reactions. After-hours trading can be less liquid, and the next regular session can produce a different verdict. The early weakness deserves attention, but it should remain separate from the completed September 9 results.

Do earnings losers stop falling?Stabilization would suggest some disappointments are being absorbed. Repeated failed recoveries and fresh lows would strengthen the defensive interpretation.

Can earnings winners keep their gains?A strong initial jump becomes more persuasive if buyers defend subsequent pullbacks. A rally that quickly disappears suggests enthusiasm is fragile.

Does weakness spread across sectors and company sizes?Continued industrial strength would support the case for selectivity. Broader selling, especially if larger reporters keep underperforming smaller ones, would make the warning more consequential.

Do downside surprises keep exceeding expectations?Repeated declines beyond the options market’s expected range would suggest investors are still underestimating the potential severity of negative reactions.

I'm also wathcing the evolving dynamics within the tech sector, specificallythe rotation out of software and into AI infrastructure stocks, to see if the momentum in names like CoreWeave and AMD can hold despite pressure on Salesforce and ServiceNow.

This shift in capital is happening against a backdrop of broader market anxiety, as my colleague Greg Michalowski noted, withthe major indices falling for a third day amid rising oil prices and surging Treasury yieldsahead of crucial CPI and PPI data.

Adding another layer of complexity to the tech outlook, investingLive's Adam Button recently warned aboutthe growing regulatory and safety fears surrounding AI development, suggesting the ultimate winners might actually be traditional "HALO" stocks that can leverage AI to improve margins, rather than the pure-play tech companies.

Relative strength:If an earnings winner holds its gains while its sector weakens, it may deserve closer attention. Losing that support would weaken the case.

Failed rallies and persistent losers:If a stock repeatedly fails to recover after disappointing results, watch whether sellers remain in control. A sustained recovery would challenge that bearish interpretation.

Sector rotation:If industrial strength persists while technology remains weak, sector ETFs may help express that difference. Their actual holdings and price behavior need to confirm the idea before it becomes a trade.

A large decline alone is not a reason to short a stock. Sharp rebounds can follow severe selloffs, making the entry point and the level at which a trade thesis fails especially important.

I would become more concerned if earnings winners began surrendering their gains at the same time that losses spread into currently resilient sectors. If losers stabilize and winners continue attracting buyers, the case for a selective market would remain stronger.

Data note: Figures are approximate and reflect observations through September 9, 2026. Rolling five-day returns are not exact post-earnings returns. After-hours reactions are preliminary. The reviewed earnings groups are not a comprehensive measure of U.S. corporate earnings.
il_articles.titre: Earnings season is turning more defensive, but the weakness is not everywhere

il_articles.contenu_fr:
La Banque de Corée établissant une distinction explicite entre l'extrême volatilité de Kospi et le positionnement à effet de levier offshore dans Samsung et SK Hynix met en évidence un risque qui échappe largement à la portée directe des régulateurs coréens, puisque les produits dérivés en question sont négociés à l'étranger. Il s’agit d’un problème très différent du boom national des ETF à effet de levier que les autorités ont déjà décidé de freiner, et qui suggère que des exigences de contrôle ou de divulgation plus poussées pourraient suivre, même si la banque centrale n’a pas proposé de mesures spécifiques jusqu’à présent. Étant donné à quel point Kospi est déjà concentré sur ces deux noms, tout renforcement de la surveillance, que ce soit du côté de l'effet de levier national ou offshore, sera probablement surveillé de près pour son potentiel à amortir les fortes fluctuations qui ont caractérisé l'indice cette année, plutôt que pour toute nouvelle immédiate sur l'évolution du marché lui-même.

---

Plus tôt :

---

La banque centrale coréenne affirme que les fluctuations brutales de son marché boursier, riche en puces, ont été alimentées par l'endettement des deux côtés du Pacifique, et pas seulement au niveau national.

Résumé :

La Banque de Corée a appelé à une surveillance plus stricte des produits dérivés étrangers liés aux fabricants de puces coréens, avertissant que leur croissance rapide risque d'amplifier la volatilité du marché boursier national. L'avertissement figure dans le rapport semestriel sur la politique monétaire de la banque centrale, remis jeudi au Parlement.

Dans le rapport, la Banque de Corée a identifié trois principaux facteurs à l'origine des fluctuations sans précédent observées dans l'indice Kospi entre janvier et juillet : la forte concentration du marché dans les actions de semi-conducteurs, le rééquilibrage des portefeuilles par les investisseurs étrangers et l'accumulation puis le dénouement de l'endettement national. La banque centrale a notamment cité le positionnement à effet de levier du fonds spéculatif américain Situational Awareness comme ayant contribué à la récente volatilité, une référence inhabituellement spécifique pour un rapport de banque centrale de ce type.

La vulnérabilité sous-jacente décrite dans le rapport est structurelle. Samsung Electronics et SK Hynix représentent ensemble plus de la moitié de la capitalisation boursière totale de la Corée, ce qui signifie que les fluctuations de l'une ou l'autre société, ou plus largement du sentiment mondial à l'égard de la demande de puces liées à l'IA, peuvent faire évoluer l'ensemble de l'indice. Cette concentration a été clairement démontrée plus tôt cette année, lorsque Kospi a plongé d’environ 40 % en six semaines, effaçant une valeur marchande estimée à 2 500 milliards de dollars et déclenchant un nombre record d’arrêts de disjoncteurs et de side-cars.

L’endettement national a joué un rôle important dans cet épisode. Les fonds négociés en bourse à effet de levier uniques liés à Samsung et SK Hynix sont devenus extrêmement populaires auprès des investisseurs particuliers, représentant à un moment donné la grande majorité du volume total des transactions de Kospi, et les pertes qui en ont résulté lorsque le marché s'est retourné ont été suffisamment graves pour que le ministre des Finances coréen ait publiquement présenté ses excuses aux investisseurs concernés. Les autorités ont depuis décidé de resserrer les règles concernant ces produits, notamment en discutant de la réduction de leurs multiples de levier.

Le côté étranger de l’équation, sur lequel se concentre le dernier rapport, est moins directement sous le contrôle des régulateurs coréens. Situational Awareness, un fonds spéculatif axé sur l'IA qui a construit une importante position à effet de levier dans SK Hynix, aurait enregistré une perte d'environ 67 % en juillet et aurait été contraint de liquider ses participations pour rembourser ses prêts, ce qui a attiré l'attention des régulateurs américains sur ses transactions et ses communications avec les prêteurs. Étant donné que ce type d'exposition se situe sur les marchés dérivés étrangers plutôt que sur les instruments supervisés directement par les régulateurs coréens, l'appel de la Banque de Corée en faveur d'une surveillance plus étroite souligne un manque de visibilité, plutôt qu'un manque de règles nationales existantes, et suggère que le débat sur la manière de gérer le risque de concentration sur le marché coréen des puces est susceptible de se poursuivre bien au-delà de ce rapport.
il_articles.contenu:
The Bank of Korea drawing an explicit line between Kospi's extreme volatility and offshore leveraged positioning in Samsung and SK Hynix highlights a risk that sits largely outside Korean regulators' direct reach, since the derivatives in question are traded overseas. That is a meaningfully different problem from the domestic leveraged ETF boom that authorities have already moved to curb, and suggests further scrutiny or disclosure requirements could follow, though the central bank has stopped short of proposing specific measures so far. Given how concentrated Kospi already is in these two names, any tightening of oversight on either the domestic or offshore leverage side is likely to be watched closely for its potential to dampen the sharp swings that have characterised the index this year, rather than for any immediate market moving news itself.

---

Earlier:

---

Korea's central bank says the wild swings in its chip heavy stock market were fuelled by leverage on both sides of the Pacific, not just at home.

Summary:

The Bank of Korea called for stronger monitoring of overseas derivatives tied to Korean chipmakers, warning that their rapid growth risks amplifying volatility in the country's domestic stock market. The warning came in the central bank's semiannual Monetary Policy Report, delivered to parliament on Thursday.

In the report, the Bank of Korea identified three main drivers behind the unprecedented swings seen in the Kospi index between January and July: the market's heavy concentration in semiconductor stocks, portfolio rebalancing by foreign investors, and the buildup and subsequent unwinding of domestic leverage. Notably, the central bank singled out leveraged positioning by Situational Awareness, a US hedge fund, as a contributor to recent volatility, an unusually specific reference for a central bank report of this kind.

The underlying vulnerability the report describes is structural. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together account for more than half of Korea's total stock market capitalisation, meaning swings in either company, or in global sentiment toward AI related chip demand more broadly, can move the entire index. That concentration was on stark display earlier this year, when Kospi plunged by roughly 40% over six weeks, wiping out an estimated $2.5 trillion in market value and triggering a record number of circuit breaker and sidecar halts.

Domestic leverage played a significant role in that episode. Single-stock leveraged exchange traded funds tied to Samsung and SK Hynix became hugely popular with retail investors, at one point accounting for the large majority of total Kospi trading volume, and the resulting losses when the market turned were severe enough that Korea's finance minister publicly apologised to affected investors. Authorities have since moved to tighten rules around those products, including discussions on lowering their leverage multiples.

The overseas side of the equation, which the latest report focuses on, is less directly within Korean regulators' control. Situational Awareness, an AI focused hedge fund that built a large leveraged position in SK Hynix, reportedly posted a loss of around 67% in July and was forced to liquidate holdings to repay loans, drawing scrutiny from US regulators over its trading and its communications with lenders. Because that kind of exposure sits in overseas derivatives markets rather than in instruments Korean regulators directly oversee, the Bank of Korea's call for closer monitoring points to a gap in visibility, rather than a lack of existing domestic rules, and suggests the debate over how to manage concentration risk in Korea's chip heavy market is likely to continue well beyond this report.
il_articles.titre_fr: La Banque de Corée associe les fluctuations sauvages de Kospi à l'effet de levier national et international
il_articles.titre: Bank of Korea links Kospi's wild swings to leverage both at home and abroad

il_articles.contenu_fr:
Pour quiconque négocie des actions coréennes, il s’agit d’une véritable expansion de la journée de négociation plutôt que d’un changement cosmétique, puisque l’appariement continu en temps réel remplace un système qui n’éliminait les ordres que toutes les 10 minutes. Cela devrait considérablement améliorer la découverte des prix après la clôture habituelle de 15h30, permettant aux traders de réagir immédiatement aux bénéfices, aux opérations sur titres ou aux gros titres mondiaux qui arrivent au cours de la nouvelle fenêtre plutôt que d'attendre les 10 minutes suivantes ou l'ouverture du lendemain.

L'exclusion des ETF et des ETN du déploiement initial mérite d'être signalée à toute personne utilisant ces instruments pour se couvrir ou obtenir une exposition sectorielle, car cette liquidité restera pour l'instant confinée à la session ordinaire.

Le contexte concurrentiel est également important : Nextrade a déjà conquis une part de marché significative en partie grâce à ses heures d'ouverture plus longues, de sorte que la liquidité dans la nouvelle fenêtre KRX en dehors des heures d'ouverture peut prendre du temps à se développer à mesure que le flux d'ordres se redistribue entre les deux sites.

---Les négociants en actions coréens sont sur le point de bénéficier de quatre heures supplémentaires de trading en temps réel par jour, alors que la bourse se bat pour suivre le rythme d'un rival en croissance rapide.

Résumé :

La Bourse de Corée lancera une nouvelle séance de négociation en temps réel après les heures d'ouverture pour les actions cotées Kospi et Kosdaq à partir du 14 septembre, prolongeant ainsi la journée de négociation effective du pays et intensifiant la concurrence avec la plateforme alternative à croissance rapide Nextrade. Cette décision fait suite à l'approbation par la Commission des services financiers de révisions des règles de fonctionnement régissant les deux marchés.

Dans le cadre du nouveau système, la séance régulière continuera à se dérouler jusqu'à 15h30, suivie d'une séance de clôture entre 15h40 et 16h. Le marché en dehors des heures d'ouverture fonctionnera alors en continu de 16h00 à 20h00, avec des ordres d'achat et de vente appariés en temps réel au fur et à mesure de leur croisement, plutôt que par lots programmés. Cela remplace l'ancien système en dehors des heures d'ouverture, qui faisait correspondre les ordres seulement toutes les 10 minutes en utilisant un mécanisme d'enchères à prix unique entre 16 heures et 18 heures, un système que les traders avaient critiqué comme étant lent à refléter les nouvelles informations arrivant sur le marché après la clôture.

Pour les traders, la portée pratique du changement compte autant que les heures de publication. La séance en dehors des heures d'ouverture couvrira la grande majorité des actions cotées et des certificats de dépôt de Kospi et Kosdaq, mais les ETF et ETN sont exclus pour le moment, la bourse citant des inquiétudes concernant la volatilité du marché. Les actions soumises au statut d'émission administrative, aux désignations d'avertissement d'investissement ou de danger d'investissement, ainsi que les titres à très faible liquidité sont également exclus. Les ordres passés en dehors des heures d'ouverture sont limités aux ordres limités uniquement, et les mêmes garanties de fourchette de prix quotidienne de 30 % et d'interruption de volatilité utilisées lors de la session ordinaire continueront de s'appliquer.

KRX a clairement indiqué que la pression concurrentielle était un facteur déterminant du changement. Nextrade, une plateforme de trading alternative lancée en mars, a déjà conquis plus de 30 % de part de marché, aidée en partie par ses propres heures de négociation plus longues et sa structure de commissions plus faible. La bourse a également souligné la tendance mondiale plus large à l'allongement des heures de négociation, notant que les principaux marchés américains, dont la Bourse de New York et le Nasdaq, ont poussé dans la même direction. KRX a déclaré avoir effectué une simulation de 23 semaines du nouveau système entre avril et début septembre pour tester la stabilité avant sa mise en service, et a indiqué qu'il avait l'intention d'examiner d'autres extensions, y compris une session préalable à la commercialisation tôt le matin, discutée précédemment, en fonction de la façon dont le lancement en dehors des heures d'ouverture se déroule.

Pour les traders actifs sur les actions coréennes, la conclusion immédiate est simple : à partir du 14 septembre, la fenêtre quotidienne effective pour réagir aux nouvelles et repositionner la plupart des titres du Kospi et du Kosdaq s'étend d'environ quatre heures, bien que la liquidité dans cette nouvelle fenêtre soit susceptible de s'accumuler progressivement à mesure que le flux d'ordres s'installe entre la Bourse de Corée et Nextrade.
il_articles.contenu:
For anyone trading Korean equities, this is a genuine expansion of the trading day rather than a cosmetic change, since real time continuous matching replaces a system that only cleared orders every 10 minutes. That should meaningfully improve price discovery after the regular 3:30pm close, letting traders react immediately to earnings, corporate actions or global headlines that land during the new window rather than waiting for the next 10 minute batch or the following day's open.

The exclusion of ETFs and ETNs from the initial rollout is worth flagging for anyone using those instruments to hedge or gain sector exposure, since that liquidity will remain confined to the regular session for now.

The competitive backdrop also matters: Nextrade has already captured meaningful market share partly on the strength of its longer hours, so liquidity in the new KRX after hours window may take time to build as order flow redistributes between the two venues.

---Korean stock traders are about to get four extra hours of real time trading a day, as the exchange fights to keep pace with a fast growing rival.

Summary:

The Korea Exchange will launch a new real time after hours trading session for Kospi and Kosdaq listed stocks from September 14, extending the country's effective trading day and stepping up competition with the fast growing alternative platform Nextrade. The move follows approval from the Financial Services Commission for revisions to the operating rules governing both markets.

Under the new system, the regular session will continue to run until 3:30pm, followed by a closing price session between 3:40pm and 4pm. The after hours market will then operate continuously from 4pm to 8pm, with buy and sell orders matched in real time as they cross, rather than in scheduled batches. This replaces the previous after hours arrangement, which matched orders only every 10 minutes using a single price auction mechanism between 4pm and 6pm, a system traders had criticised as slow to reflect fresh information reaching the market after the close.

For traders, the practical scope of the change matters as much as the headline hours. The after hours session will cover the large majority of Kospi and Kosdaq listed shares and depositary receipts, but ETFs and ETNs are excluded for now, with the exchange citing concerns about market volatility. Stocks under administrative issue status, investment warning or investment danger designations, and ultra low liquidity names are also excluded. Orders during the after hours window are restricted to limit orders only, and the same 30% daily price band and volatility interruption safeguards used in the regular session will continue to apply.

KRX has been explicit that competitive pressure is a driving factor behind the change. Nextrade, an alternative trading platform that launched in March, has already captured more than 30% market share, helped in part by its own longer trading hours and lower commission structure. The exchange also pointed to the broader global trend of extended trading hours, noting that major US markets including the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq have been pushing in the same direction. KRX said it ran a 23 week simulation of the new system between April and early September to test stability before going live, and indicated it intends to review further extensions, including a previously discussed early morning pre-market session, based on how the after hours launch performs.

For traders active in Korean equities, the immediate takeaway is straightforward: from September 14, the effective daily window for reacting to news and repositioning in most Kospi and Kosdaq names extends by roughly four hours, though liquidity in that new window is likely to build gradually as order flow settles between the Korea Exchange and Nextrade.
il_articles.titre_fr: Korea Exchange lancera le trading en temps réel jusqu'à 20 heures à partir du 14 septembre
il_articles.titre: Korea Exchange to launch real time trading through to 8pm from September 14

il_articles.contenu_fr:
Un engagement de cette ampleur, s’il était un jour légiféré, représenterait une expansion significative de la dette à un moment où les inquiétudes concernant le déficit et les émissions du Trésor pèsent déjà sur les marchés obligataires. Pour l’instant, la promesse est conditionnée à une victoire républicaine en novembre et ne comporte aucun mécanisme de financement ni voie législative, il est donc peu probable qu’elle fasse bouger les marchés à court terme.

La lecture la plus pertinente pour les traders pourrait être ce qu'elle indique sur la stratégie politique de l'administration à l'approche de la mi-mandat, utilisant les paiements directs comme réponse aux inquiétudes du public concernant le coût de la vie, plutôt que toute implication immédiate en matière de politique fiscale ou monétaire.

---

Plus tôt :

---

Trump fait miroiter un chèque de 5 000 dollars à chaque adulte américain comme prix à payer pour maintenir les Républicains à la tête du Congrès.

Résumé :

Le président Trump a déclaré mercredi à ses partisans lors du premier congrès de mi-mandat du Parti républicain à Dallas qu'il verserait un dividende de 5 000 dollars à chaque citoyen américain adulte si les républicains conservaient le contrôle des deux chambres du Congrès lors des élections de novembre.

S’adressant à la foule, Trump a présenté cet engagement comme une récompense directement liée au résultat des élections de mi-mandat. "Si les républicains remportent la Chambre des représentants et le Sénat des États-Unis, tous deux, je verserai un dividende de 5 000 dollars à chaque citoyen adulte des États-Unis d'Amérique", a-t-il déclaré, comparant cela à une société qui distribuerait une distribution en espèces à ses actionnaires. La seule condition qu’il a précisée était que l’argent devait être dépensé aux États-Unis. Il a qualifié la proposition de « dividende Trump ».

Avec environ 270 millions d’adultes dans le pays, cet engagement coûterait environ 1,35 billion de dollars s’il était un jour mis en œuvre. Trump n’a pas expliqué comment les paiements seraient financés, ni décrit un quelconque processus législatif permettant de transformer la promesse en un véritable programme. Un tel paiement nécessiterait probablement l’autorisation du Congrès, ce qui signifie que son sort dépendrait fortement de la composition du Congrès après la mi-mandat, le résultat même que l’engagement est censé influencer.

Ce n’est pas la première fois que Trump propose un paiement direct financé, du moins en théorie, par les recettes douanières. En 2025, il a promu un dividende tarifaire de 2 000 dollars pour les Américains, une idée qui n’a jamais abouti à l’envoi d’un programme ou de paiements réels. Le nouveau chiffre de 5 000 $ représente plus du double de la proposition précédente. Il s'agit également d'un montant distinct du « dividende du guerrier » de 1 776 dollars que Trump avait précédemment promis aux militaires américains et qui, selon lui, serait financé par les recettes douanières.

Que l'engagement de mercredi se traduise par une véritable poussée législative, ou reste un sujet de discussion de campagne similaire à celui de 2025, dépendra probablement du résultat des élections de novembre et des négociations ultérieures au Congrès. Pour l’instant, cette promesse ajoute une nouvelle idée budgétaire à grande échelle au débat politique à l’approche des élections de mi-mandat, même si les questions sur le financement et la faisabilité restent sans réponse.
il_articles.contenu:
A pledge of this scale, if it were ever legislated, would represent a meaningful debt expansion at a moment when concerns about the deficit and Treasury issuance are already weighing on bond markets. For now, the promise is conditional on a Republican sweep in November and carries no funding mechanism or legislative pathway, so it is unlikely to move markets in the near term.

The more relevant read for traders may be what it signals about the administration's political strategy heading into the midterms, using direct payments as a response to public concern over the cost of living, rather than any immediate fiscal or monetary policy implication.

---

Earlier:

---

Trump is dangling a $5,000 check to every American adult as the price of keeping Republicans in charge of Congress.

Summary:

President Trump told supporters at the Republican Party's first midterm convention in Dallas on Wednesday that he would issue a $5,000 dividend to every adult US citizen if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress in November's elections.

Speaking to the crowd, Trump framed the pledge as a reward tied directly to the outcome of the midterms. "If the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States of America for $5,000," he said, likening it to a company issuing a cash distribution to its shareholders. The only condition he specified was that the money would need to be spent within the United States. He referred to the proposal as the "Trump Dividend."

With an estimated 270 million adults in the country, the pledge would cost in the region of $1.35 trillion if it were ever implemented. Trump did not explain how the payments would be funded, nor did he outline any legislative process for turning the promise into an actual program. Any such payment would likely require congressional authorization, meaning its fate would depend heavily on the makeup of Congress after the midterms, the very outcome the pledge is meant to influence.

This is not the first time Trump has floated a direct payment funded, at least in concept, by tariff revenue. In 2025 he promoted a $2,000 tariff dividend for Americans, an idea that never resulted in an actual program or payments being sent. The new $5,000 figure is more than double that earlier proposal. It is also separate from the $1,776 "warrior dividend" Trump previously promised to US military service members, which he said would be funded through tariff revenue.

Whether Wednesday's pledge translates into a genuine legislative push, or remains a campaign talking point similar to its 2025 predecessor, will likely depend on the November election result and on subsequent negotiations in Congress. For now, the promise adds a new, large scale fiscal idea to the political conversation heading into the midterms, even as questions about funding and feasibility remain unanswered.
il_articles.titre_fr: Trump lie sa promesse de paiement de 5 000 dollars à un scrutin républicain complet à mi-mandat
il_articles.titre: Trump ties $5,000 payment promise to a full Republican midterm sweep

il_articles.contenu:
Masu's comments add to a hawkish tilt already building among BOJ board members ahead of the September meeting, reinforcing market expectations that a hike is likely, indeed abasically set in stone. His specific focus on the weak yen having a bigger inflation impact than in the past, alongside concern about producer prices feeding through to consumer inflation more than historically,gives the yen some supporton the margin, since it signals the board is not just reacting to headline energy costs but building a broader case for policy normalisation.

With the policy rate already described as approaching the estimated neutral range, the more market sensitive signal here may be Masu's comment that the BOJ could be forced to raise rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, which raises the stakes around upcoming data releases between now and the meeting, and beyond.

---

Earlier:

---

A BOJ board member who has already called for early hikes says the case for continuing to raise rates keeps getting stronger, not weaker.

Summary:

Bank of Japan board member Kazuyuki Masu said underlying inflation remains below the central bank's 2% target but is now quite close to it, adding that the BOJ is expected to continue raising interest rates given how accommodative financial conditions remain. His comments come ahead of the BOJ's next policy meeting on September 17 and 18, which markets widely expect to produce a further rate hike.

Masu, a former chief financial officer at trading house Mitsubishi Corp, joined the BOJ board in July 2025, filling a seat traditionally reserved for a business executive. He is generally regarded as one of the more hawkish members of the current board. He voted to keep rates unchanged at the BOJ's April meeting, but said the following month that he believed rates should rise as soon as possible provided there were no clear signs of an economic slowdown, so his comments are consistent with that stance rather than a shift in it.

On the substance, Masu said the pace and timing of further rate increases would depend on the likelihood of achieving the BOJ's baseline inflation projections, alongside risks tied to oil prices, AI related demand and currency fluctuations. He said the most important consideration is avoiding a sharp overshoot of underlying inflation above the 2% target. He also addressed the current run up in energy costs directly, saying that while a rise in fuel and chemical goods prices could prove to be a one off shock, it may still have a broader impact on prices through distribution costs, and separately flagged concern that rising costs stemming from the Middle East conflict could push up overall prices as a lasting trend rather than a temporary one.

Masu pointed to several additional pressures worth watching, including a recent 7% spike in producer prices, which he said could feed through to consumer inflation more than it has historically, alongside an expected reacceleration in food prices that he described as potentially key to the long term inflation outlook. He also said the weak yen is having a larger impact on inflation than in the past and therefore warrants close attention, and separately noted no sign yet that recent rate hikes are denting corporate appetite for funds, adding he was watching for signs that corporate investment could be overheating.

On the policy framework itself, Masu said Japan is no longer in deflation and that the BOJ must move its real interest rate out of negative territory as soon as possible. With the policy rate now approaching the BOJ's estimated neutral range, he said the central bank needs to watch price, job and financial conditions carefully, and warned that if inflation accelerates, the BOJ could be forced to raise rates more rapidly than currently anticipated. He also flagged a separate, longer term question facing the BOJ over which maturity range of Japanese government bonds it should continue holding as it considers the desirable size of its balance sheet.
il_articles.titre: Weak yen, oil costs and food prices in focus as BOJ's Masu talks hikes

What the September futures rollover means for ES and NQ traders

Every quarter, traders in the E-mini S&P 500 (ES) and E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) go through a ritual that catches out newer participants more often than it should: the futures rollover. With the next quarterly expiry falling on the third Friday of September, this is a good moment to explain what is actually happening, and why it matters even if you never intend to hold a contract into expiry.

Why futures expire at all

Unlike a stock, which exists indefinitely, a futures contract is a promise to buy or sell an underlying asset at a set price on a set date. Index futures like ES and NQ follow a quarterly cycle: March, June, September and December, often labeled H, M, U and Z after their delivery month codes. Each contract has a finite life. As it approaches expiry, exchanges and clearing firms need traders to either close their position, take (or make) delivery in some form, or shift that position into the next contract in the cycle. For cash settled index futures like ES and NQ, there is no physical delivery, but the contract still stops trading and settles to a final price, so an open position has to move to the next quarter one way or another.

Spotting the roll: volume and open interest

The rollover is not a single moment dictated by the exchange. It is a gradual shift in where trading activity actually sits. In the days leading up to expiry, volume and open interest in the front month contract (currently the September, or U, contract) start draining away into the next quarter's contract (December, or Z). Most professional traders and data providers use a volume crossover as the practical signal that the roll has happened, the point where the back month contract starts trading more volume than the front month. For ES and NQ, this crossover typically lands around a week or so before the actual expiry date, though the exact timing can shift depending on market conditions.

On timing specifically

CME's own convention for equity index futures, per itsofficial roll dates page, is that the roll date falls on the Monday prior to the third Friday of the expiration month. With expiry on Friday, September 18 this quarter, that puts the roll date on Monday, September 14, not today. After that Monday, it becomes customary to treat the December contract as the new "lead month" for quoting and display purposes on CME Globex, since the nearer September contract is close to expiring and will trade with thinner liquidity. As always, you're free to roll your own position whenever you choose, comparing volume and open interest between the two contracts is the practical way to judge whether the market has actually made the switch yet.

Volume Crossover Dynamics

While CME standardizes data switching Monday, the physical volume shift often spans a "window". Traders execution-sensitive to order book depth should closely watch actual contract volume before placing market orders.

Why the two contracts do not trade at the same price

A common source of confusion is why the September and December contracts are not priced identically. The difference, sometimes called the futures roll spread, reflects the cost of carry, essentially the interest earned on the underlying value of the index minus the dividends expected to be paid out by index constituents before the next contract expires. In a normal environment, financial futures trade at a slight premium to the cash index in the nearer months, and that premium can shift between contracts as dividend expectations and interest rates change. This is not a market inefficiency to be traded on its own, it is a structural feature of how index futures are priced, but it does mean that a continuous chart built from stitching contracts together needs to account for that gap, or it will show an artificial jump at every rollover.

What happens if you do nothing

If a position is left open into the final days before expiry, liquidity in the front month contract thins out noticeably as volume migrates to the new contract. Bid ask spreads widen, and depending on the broker, there may be automatic position transfers or forced closures ahead of the last trading day, since most retail and even institutional traders have no interest in holding an index future to actual cash settlement. The practical lesson is simple: know your broker's specific rollover policy and don't assume a position will simply carry itself over.

A note for anyone using tick or volume based charts

For traders using bar types built from volume or tick activity rather than time, such as Renko style constructions, the rollover carries an extra wrinkle. Continuous data feeds have to decide how to splice the tick or volume history of the old contract into the new one, and because the two contracts are trading at slightly different price levels around the roll, a poorly handled splice can distort bar formation right at the transition, particularly for compression heavy bar types where a handful of ticks either side of the roll can matter. It is worth checking, at least once a quarter, that a charting platform's back adjustment method has not introduced an artificial gap or a run of unusually large or small bars exactly at the rollover point.

The takeaway

The rollover itself is not a dramatic event, but it is a useful quarterly reminder that a futures contract is a living, expiring instrument, not a permanent proxy for the index it tracks. Watching the volume crossover, understanding why the new contract is priced differently, and checking how continuous charts handle the transition are small habits that prevent unpleasant surprises when the calendar quietly turns over again in December.
il_articles.titre: What the September futures rollover means for traders, ES and NQ as examples

il_articles.contenu_fr:
Alors qu'ING envisage une hausse de 25 points de base pour tous les scénarios envisagés, la réunion d'aujourd'hui portera probablement moins sur la décision de taux elle-même que sur le langage et les projections qui l'accompagnent. L'écart établi par ING entre ses résultats les plus conciliants et les plus bellicistes, l'EUR/USD allant de 1,150 à 1,168 et le rendement du Bund à 10 ans de 3,30 % à 3,45 %, indique un risque bidirectionnel significatif autour de la conférence de presse plutôt que de la décision elle-même. Étant donné que l'euro et le Bund se situent actuellement près du milieu de cette fourchette, à 1,161 et 3,40% respectivement, le positionnement dans l'annonce semble raisonnablement équilibré, laissant la possibilité d'un mouvement brusque une fois que le ton des orientations deviendra clair.

---

Plus tôt :

---

ING pense que le changement de taux de la BCE aujourd'hui est proche d'une formalité, c'est le ton des orientations qui fera réellement bouger les marchés.

Résumé :

ING s'attend à ce que la Banque centrale européenne augmente son taux de dépôt de 25 points de base lors de la réunion d'aujourd'hui, quelle que soit la direction dans laquelle le ton des orientations qui l'accompagnent change, selon un cadre de scénarios publié par la banque avant la décision. Le taux de dépôt actuel s'élève à 2,25 %, la BCE maintenant une approche dépendante des données, réunion par réunion avant l'annonce.

La note de la banque, illustrée dans un graphique d'accompagnement, présente quatre résultats possibles autour de l'inflation, de la croissance et du ton de l'orientation des taux d'intérêt. Dans sa position actuelle, ING voit des risques à la hausse pour l'inflation liés à la hausse des prix de l'énergie et à la possibilité d'effets de second tour, tandis que les risques de croissance restent orientés à la baisse à court terme en raison de la guerre au Moyen-Orient.

À l'extrémité accommodante du spectre, le scénario très accommodant d'ING prévoit que la BCE procède à la hausse attendue tout en signalant une pause prolongée et en exprimant ses inquiétudes sur les conditions du marché obligataire, une combinaison que la banque associe à un euro plus faible proche de 1,150 et à un rendement du Bund à 10 ans autour de 3,30 %. Le scénario de base d'ING se situe juste au-dessus de celui d'un scénario de hausse accommodante, dans lequel les projections d'inflation sont révisées légèrement à la hausse sans modifier l'équilibre plus large des risques, les prévisions de croissance s'améliorent alors que les risques à la baisse persistent, et les décideurs politiques n'offrent qu'une légère résistance aux prix du marché tout en gardant leurs options ouvertes. Ce scénario est associé à un EUR/USD proche de 1,157 et à un rendement du Bund autour de 3,35 %.

S'orientant vers une approche plus belliciste, un scénario neutre verrait la BCE reconnaître que la dernière escalade dans la région ajoute un nouveau risque d'inflation à la hausse, tout en traitant les risques de croissance comme plus équilibrés suite à l'amélioration des projections, et en signalant qu'une autre hausse dans les mois à venir reste possible. ING associe ce résultat à un EUR/USD autour de 1,163 et à un rendement du Bund proche de 3,40 %, proche du niveau actuel de négociation des deux titres. Dans son scénario le plus agressif, ING voit la BCE reconnaître que l'impact de l'inflation pourrait être plus important qu'on ne le pensait initialement, ce qui nécessiterait une action politique continue, parallèlement à une révision à la hausse plus importante que prévu des projections de croissance, avec des allusions claires à une nouvelle hausse en octobre et potentiellement au-delà. Ce résultat atteint les niveaux les plus élevés du cadre d'ING, avec un EUR/USD proche de 1,168 et un rendement du Bund autour de 3,45 %.

Alors que l'euro et le Bund se négocient actuellement au plus près du scénario neutre d'ING, le cadre de la banque suggère que les marchés sont déjà enclins à penser que la hausse d'aujourd'hui s'accompagnera d'un ton plus ferme plutôt que d'un ton accommodant, laissant la possibilité d'une réaction plus large si les orientations de la BCE se rapprochent finalement de l'une ou l'autre extrémité de la fourchette d'ING.
il_articles.contenu:
With ING pencilling in a 25 basis point hike across every scenario it considers, today's meeting is likely to be less about the rate decision itself and more about the accompanying language and projections. The spread ING lays out between its most dovish and most hawkish outcomes, EUR/USD ranging from 1.150 to 1.168 and the 10 year Bund yield from 3.30% to 3.45%, points to meaningful two way risk around the press conference rather than the decision itself. Given the euro and Bund currently sit close to the middle of that range, at 1.161 and 3.40% respectively, positioning into the announcement looks reasonably balanced, leaving room for a sharp move once the tone of the guidance becomes clear.

---

Earlier:

---

ING thinks the ECB's rate move today is close to a formality, it is the tone of the guidance that will actually move markets.

Summary:

ING expects the European Central Bank to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points at today's meeting regardless of which way the tone of the accompanying guidance breaks, according to a scenario framework the bank published ahead of the decision. The current depo rate stands at 2.25%, with the ECB maintaining a data dependent, meeting by meeting approach heading into the announcement.

The bank's note, illustrated in an accompanying graphic, sets out four possible outcomes built around inflation, growth and the tone of interest rate guidance. In the current stance, ING sees upside risks to inflation from higher energy prices and the possibility of second round effects, while growth risks remain tilted to the downside in the near term because of the war in the Middle East.

At the dovish end of the spectrum, ING's very dovish scenario has the ECB delivering the expected hike while signalling a prolonged pause and voicing concern about bond market conditions, a combination the bank associates with a weaker euro near 1.150 and a 10 year Bund yield around 3.30%. ING's own base case sits just above that in a dovish hike scenario, where inflation projections are revised slightly higher without shifting the broader balance of risk, growth forecasts improve while downside risks linger, and policymakers offer only a slight pushback against market pricing while keeping their options open. That scenario is associated with EUR/USD near 1.157 and a Bund yield around 3.35%.

Moving toward the hawkish end, a neutral scenario would see the ECB acknowledge that the latest escalation in the region is adding fresh upside inflation risk, while treating growth risks as more balanced following improved projections, and signalling that another hike in the coming months remains possible. ING pairs that outcome with EUR/USD around 1.163 and a Bund yield near 3.40%, close to where both currently trade. In its most hawkish scenario, ING sees the ECB acknowledging that the inflation impact may be larger than initially thought, requiring continued policy action, alongside a bigger than expected upward revision to growth projections, with clear hints of a further hike in October and potentially beyond. That outcome carries the highest levels in ING's framework, with EUR/USD near 1.168 and the Bund yield around 3.45%.

With the euro and Bund currently trading closest to ING's neutral case, the bank's framework suggests markets are already leaning toward the view that today's hike will come with a firmer tone rather than a dovish one, leaving scope for a larger reaction if the ECB's guidance ultimately lands closer to either extreme of ING's range.
